source.title: A Jailbreak Success Coordinate Outside the Refusal Subspace: Decodable Before Generation, Reachable from the Input

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; it is an under-review ICLR 2027 submission.
record.tranche_reason: The study refines the single-direction account by separating a coordinate that predicts which jailbreak variant succeeds from the refusal-direction span whose intervention more strongly changes attack success. Its results qualify what refusal-direction interventions establish about attack coverage.
record.gate_note: The study includes interventions on eleven published refusal-direction estimates, including the difference-in-means direction, and compares their effects with an orthogonal success-fitted coordinate. Reported aggregate intervention results do not isolate the difference-in-means direction, so they cannot establish its individual effect. The attack-search success rates are results of the paper's own optimized methods, not evidence that attacks generally suppress the refusal direction; they are not catalogued as claim-version results. Harmless-request addition, general capability preservation, weight-edit abliteration, and training against ablation are not tested.
record.test_reason: The study ablates each of eleven published refusal directions, including the DIM direction, at every layer against magnitude-matched random controls. This bears on V1's ablation claim. It also measures whether successful jailbreak variants separate on those directions, which bears on V3's claim that attacks work through the direction. It finds weak separation on DIM and most attack displacement outside the refusal span.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the success coordinate can be driven from the input as a search objective, yielding working suffix, template and rephrase attacks. Also add that searches using a refusal direction as fitness give no consistent ordering of success.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses success-versus-failure variants of the same harmful request to fit a difference-in-means direction, then orthogonalizes it against a span of eleven published refusal-direction estimates. It does not reproduce the original single-direction harmless-versus-harmful contrast as its central measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Discrimination is lower below relative depth 0.3 and reaches a plateau at later depths; the direction is refit at each layer. Outcomes also vary by intervention starting point and model; Gemma-3-1B reverses the main set-A/set-C comparison, Mistral-7B shows no intervention effect, and Gemma-3-4B is unmeasurable under the degeneration criterion. Cross-dataset transfer is reported with model and augmentation family held fixed.

fits_no_version.finding: A success-versus-failure direction orthogonal to the refusal span predicts which jailbreak variant succeeds (AUC 0.903) and transfers across datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak success is decodable pre-generation from a coordinate outside the refusal-direction span.

record.code_released: not stated (the authors say they will release code upon publication)
record.problems: The single DIM intervention effect is not separately reported in text. The intervention significance tests cover four models; one is unmeasurable because of degeneration. The magnitude-matched random control itself raises success by a median +0.063 on HarmBench-standard and +0.105 on AdvBench-520 relative to no intervention. The authors state that the interventions do not isolate the causal role of the orthogonal complement, and that input searches move other representational features.
record.rows_left_out: Search success-rate tables for the paper's own coordinate-optimized suffix, template, and rephrase attacks were not entered as claim-version rows: these are induced results of the study's methods rather than direct tests of the listed refusal-direction claims. Individual DIM intervention outcomes in Figures 6–7 were not separately extracted because the text does not assign their plotted values to DIM in prose.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to harmless requests to induce refusal; preservation of general capability; DIM's ablation effect isolated from the other 10 directions (in figures only).
Whether refusal is affine, a cone or multi-directional (the 11 directions are only pooled).
All (dataset transfer concerns the success direction).

missing.what: Share of attack displacement lying in the refusal span never exceeds 0.405; DIM alone covers 0.182 (11 axes 0.225).
Successful rows move farther inside the refusal subspace than failed rows (positive in 23/24 combinations for three families; PAP 4/8).
Searches that suppress DIM as their objective: suffix ASR 0.290 overall vs random 0.194; template spread with −DIM fitness −0.21 overall (no ordering).
Per-direction (including DIM alone) ablation effects per model and dataset.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Refusal-direction ablation results pool 11 directions; DIM is isolated only in figures. The magnitude-matched random control alone raises success by +0.063 to +0.105 median.

versions.untested_parts: The paper intervenes on the published difference-in-means refusal direction as part of a set of refusal directions, but does not report its effect separately in text. It does not test adding the direction to harmless requests or preservation of general capability.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
The study does not test whether attacks suppress the refusal direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
The refusal-direction span is used as a comparison object, but the study does not establish whether refusal itself is affine, a cone, or a dominant direction plus others.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
The reported cross-dataset transfer concerns a success-failure direction, not transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
No variation in refusal training or training stage is tested.

relation.reason: It ablates and restores 11 published refusal directions, DIM included, against magnitude-matched random controls, and measures success separation on them.

tranche.reason: The study argues, with results, that refusal directions mediate behavior under intervention but are not what separates successful from failed attacks. That means V3 needs restating, and V1 holds only partly (null on Mistral-7B).

source_check.notes: The text never says the models are instruct/chat versions or gives checkpoint versions. The refusal side pools 11 directions; DIM-only cells appear only in Figs 6-7. The authors' 'no consistent ordering' for refusal-direction fitness holds on the template surface. On the rephrase surface the -DIM spread is +0.36 and -RDO +0.52 (Overall), against +0.62 for û⊥sf. A suffix search lowering DIM reaches 0.033 on Llama-3.1-8B but 0.460 on Mistral-7B (Table 2). The OpenReview footer addresses human reviewers and is not an injection. The pack listed verdicts without [lN] ids, so l1-l4 are assigned in listed order.

statements.correction: Mistral-7B: result fails, room to ceiling at least 0.30; set A has 3 of 48 combinations as support, 4 unmeasurable, rest null. Starting points are set A (original harmful request) and set C (failed augmentation). Significant in 2 of 4 tested models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B). Gemma-3-4B unmeasurable: output degenerates even under random-direction moves. Mistral-7B version not stated.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but 'no significant change' slightly overstates: in the Mistral-7B paragraph 3 of 48 set-A combinations are significant support. The null also covers ablation from the plain harmful request (set A), not only jailbreak variants. The effect pools 11 refusal directions rather than isolating DIM.

statements.correction: Set B (component in a successful augmentation returned to its unaugmented value) is weaker than ablation: markedly fewer combinations exceed their matched random control, and Llama-3.1-8B has opposite-sign combinations. The text gives no number.
statements.problem: The statement is cut off before its claim about this study. The cited R7 shows a weaker, not absent, restoration effect, which fits limits_scope rather than challenges.

statements.correction: DIM median paired AUC 0.7421 vs 0.6269 for random directions, over 80 combinations (10 models, 2 datasets, 4 families), last prompt position, relative depth 0.8, sign fitted per training fold. The in-span component ΠR ûsf reaches 0.8255. R holds at most 0.405 of the displacement norm.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but DIM separates above random, and the AUC sign is fitted on the training fold. So this does not show attacks succeeding without suppressing the direction. It shows that DIM separates success from failure only weakly.

statements.correction: For V3 this study gives weak DIM separation (0.7421 vs random 0.6269) and a weak set-B restoration effect. A template search using -DIM as fitness gives a spread that flips sign across models. The robustness-training clause is untested.
statements.problem: The visible text, cut off, makes no claim about this study, and no rows from it are cited.
